lessons.title: Epidemiology and Pathophysiology of Hip and Femur Fractures

content.intro: Hip and femur fractures are a significant cause of morbidity and mortality in the elderly population. The incidence of hip fractures is expected to increase with the aging population, with approximately 1.6 million hip fractures occurring worldwide each year. The pathophysiology of hip and femur fractures involves a combination of factors, including osteoporosis, falls, and trauma. Osteoporosis is a major risk factor for hip fractures, with the majority of hip fractures occurring in individuals with osteoporosis. The economic burden of hip and femur fractures is substantial, with estimated annual costs exceeding $10 billion in the United States alone.

sections.heading: Epidemiology of Hip and Femur Fractures
sections.text: The epidemiology of hip and femur fractures is complex and multifactorial. The incidence of hip fractures increases with age, with the majority of hip fractures occurring in individuals over the age of 65. Women are more likely to experience hip fractures than men, with a female-to-male ratio of approximately 2:1. The incidence of hip fractures also varies by geographic location, with higher rates of hip fractures observed in Scandinavian countries. The ESC 2019 guideline recommends that individuals with a history of falls or osteoporosis be screened for hip fracture risk.

sections.heading: Pathophysiology of Hip and Femur Fractures
sections.text: The pathophysiology of hip and femur fractures involves a combination of factors, including osteoporosis, falls, and trauma. Osteoporosis is a major risk factor for hip fractures, with the majority of hip fractures occurring in individuals with osteoporosis. The AHA 2020 guideline recommends that individuals with osteoporosis be treated with bisphosphonates, such as alendronate 70mg weekly or risedronate 35mg weekly. The NICE 2017 guideline recommends that individuals with a history of falls or osteoporosis be referred to a falls prevention program.

sections.heading: Risk Factors for Hip and Femur Fractures
sections.text: Several risk factors have been identified for hip and femur fractures, including osteoporosis, falls, and trauma. The landmark FIT trial demonstrated that treatment with teriparatide 20mcg daily reduced the risk of hip fractures by 50% in individuals with osteoporosis. The ESC 2019 guideline recommends that individuals with a history of falls or osteoporosis be treated with calcium and vitamin D supplements, such as calcium 500mg daily and vitamin D 800 IU daily.

lessons.title: Clinical Presentation of Hip and Femur Fractures

content.intro: The clinical presentation of hip and femur fractures can vary depending on the location and severity of the fracture. Individuals with hip fractures may present with hip pain, difficulty walking, and limited range of motion. Femur fractures may present with thigh pain, swelling, and deformity. A thorough physical examination and diagnostic imaging are essential for accurate diagnosis and treatment.

sections.heading: Symptoms of Hip and Femur Fractures
sections.text: The symptoms of hip and femur fractures can vary depending on the location and severity of the fracture. Hip fractures may present with hip pain, difficulty walking, and limited range of motion. Femur fractures may present with thigh pain, swelling, and deformity. The AHA 2020 guideline recommends that individuals with suspected hip or femur fractures undergo prompt diagnostic imaging, such as X-ray or CT scan.

sections.heading: Physical Examination of Hip and Femur Fractures
sections.text: A thorough physical examination is essential for accurate diagnosis and treatment of hip and femur fractures. The physical examination should include assessment of hip and knee range of motion, strength, and sensation. The NICE 2017 guideline recommends that individuals with suspected hip or femur fractures undergo a thorough physical examination, including assessment of cognitive function and mobility.

sections.heading: Diagnostic Imaging of Hip and Femur Fractures
sections.text: Diagnostic imaging is essential for accurate diagnosis and treatment of hip and femur fractures. X-ray and CT scan are commonly used imaging modalities for diagnosis of hip and femur fractures. The ESC 2019 guideline recommends that individuals with suspected hip or femur fractures undergo prompt diagnostic imaging, such as X-ray or CT scan, to confirm the diagnosis and guide treatment.

lessons.title: Investigations and Diagnosis of Hip and Femur Fractures

content.intro: The diagnosis of hip and femur fractures requires a combination of clinical evaluation, diagnostic imaging, and laboratory tests. X-ray and CT scan are commonly used imaging modalities for diagnosis of hip and femur fractures. Laboratory tests, such as complete blood count and electrolyte panel, may be ordered to rule out underlying conditions.

sections.heading: Imaging Modalities for Hip and Femur Fractures
sections.text: X-ray and CT scan are commonly used imaging modalities for diagnosis of hip and femur fractures. X-ray is typically the first-line imaging modality, with CT scan used for further evaluation of complex fractures. The NICE 2017 guideline recommends that individuals with suspected hip or femur fractures undergo prompt diagnostic imaging, such as X-ray or CT scan, to confirm the diagnosis and guide treatment.

sections.heading: Laboratory Tests for Hip and Femur Fractures
sections.text: Laboratory tests, such as complete blood count and electrolyte panel, may be ordered to rule out underlying conditions, such as infection or bleeding disorders. The AHA 2020 guideline recommends that individuals with suspected hip or femur fractures undergo laboratory tests, such as complete blood count and electrolyte panel, to rule out underlying conditions.

sections.heading: Classification of Hip and Femur Fractures
sections.text: Hip and femur fractures can be classified based on location, severity, and type of fracture. The Garden classification system is commonly used to classify hip fractures, with type I fractures being non-displaced and type IV fractures being displaced. The ESC 2019 guideline recommends that individuals with hip or femur fractures undergo classification of the fracture to guide treatment.

lessons.title: Treatment and Management of Hip and Femur Fractures

content.intro: The treatment and management of hip and femur fractures depend on the location, severity, and type of fracture. Non-surgical management, such as pain control and physical therapy, may be used for non-displaced fractures. Surgical management, such as internal fixation or arthroplasty, may be used for displaced fractures.

sections.heading: Non-Surgical Management of Hip and Femur Fractures
sections.text: Non-surgical management, such as pain control and physical therapy, may be used for non-displaced fractures. The AHA 2020 guideline recommends that individuals with non-displaced hip or femur fractures undergo non-surgical management, including pain control and physical therapy. The NICE 2017 guideline recommends that individuals with non-displaced hip or femur fractures undergo a structured rehabilitation program, including physical therapy and occupational therapy.

sections.heading: Surgical Management of Hip and Femur Fractures
sections.text: Surgical management, such as internal fixation or arthroplasty, may be used for displaced fractures. The ESC 2019 guideline recommends that individuals with displaced hip or femur fractures undergo surgical management, such as internal fixation or arthroplasty, to restore function and mobility. The landmark FIT trial demonstrated that treatment with teriparatide 20mcg daily reduced the risk of hip fractures by 50% in individuals with osteoporosis.

sections.heading: Complications and Prognosis of Hip and Femur Fractures
sections.text: Complications of hip and femur fractures can include infection, bleeding, and nerve damage. The prognosis of hip and femur fractures depends on the location, severity, and type of fracture, as well as the individual's overall health status. The AHA 2020 guideline recommends that individuals with hip or femur fractures undergo regular follow-up to monitor for complications and adjust treatment as needed.
